slides.title: 4 myths about [[p*rn withdrawal.]]
slides.sub: A 7-day study found it's usually not what people fear.

slides.title: No [[detox]] crash
slides.body: In a randomized study (Fernandez et al., 2023), 176 regular p*rn users were split into a 7-day abstinence group and a control group. The abstinence group didn't report more cravings or withdrawal-type symptoms overall. Students, one week — very heavy users may feel more.

slides.title: Myths [[1–2]]
items: "Quitting p*rn will feel like a drug detox." For most regular users in that study, it didn't.
"The first week is unbearable." Hard, maybe. Unbearable, usually not.

slides.title: Myths [[3–4]]
items: "If I feel bad, it's withdrawal." It may be stress or boredom p*rn used to cover.
"I can't quit without suffering." Fear of the pain often keeps people stuck longer than the pain.

slides.title: What this [[means]]
items: Stop waiting for the "right time" to face it.
Expect habit urges, not torture.
Notice the feelings p*rn was covering — and deal with them.
Get help if your use feels truly out of control.

carousels.name: 5 kinds of rest that beat p*rn

slides.title: 5 kinds of rest [[that beat p*rn.]]
slides.sub: P*rn feels like rest. It isn't.

slides.title: Rest [[1–2]]
items: Physical: sleep, a nap, stretching — not lying in bed scrolling.
Mental: 10 minutes with no input. No phone, no p*rn, no podcast.

slides.title: Rest [[3–4]]
items: Social: time with people who don't drain you.
Sensory: lights down, screens off, quiet room.

slides.title: [[Creative]] rest
slides.body: Music, drawing, cooking, walking somewhere beautiful. Things that fill you up — instead of emptying you out like p*rn does.

slides.title: Find your [[rest]]
items: Ask: what kind of tired am I?
Pick the matching rest from this list.
Do it for 15 minutes before reaching for your phone.
Compare how you feel after it vs. after p*rn.

carousels.name: 3 things to forgive yourself for as you quit p*rn (NNN)

slides.title: 3 things to forgive yourself for [[as you quit p*rn this month.]]
slides.sub: Don't carry the shame into December.

slides.title: The [[years]]
slides.body: The time you spent on p*rn is gone. Replaying it won't bring it back. Learn from it. Then let it go.

slides.title: The [[slips]]
slides.body: Maybe this month wasn't perfect. Every restart still counts. You're still here.

slides.title: The [[secrets]]
slides.body: The things you hid, the lies you told about p*rn. Forgiving yourself doesn't mean it didn't matter. It means you're ready to do better.

slides.title: How to [[let go]]
items: Write it down — then close the notebook.
Say it to someone you trust.
Make amends if you need to.
If the shame feels too heavy, talk to a professional or a helpline.
slides.note: Send this to someone who's too hard on themselves ↗

slides.title:
Let go of the past.

carousels.name: 4 ways you're making quitting p*rn harder than it needs to be

slides.title: 4 ways you're making quitting p*rn [[harder than it needs to be.]]
slides.sub: Some of the struggle is self-inflicted.

slides.title: You keep [[backdoors]] open
slides.body: Blocker off "for a minute." A saved account "just in case." You can't quit p*rn with one foot out the door.

slides.title: You wait for [[motivation]]
slides.body: Motivation shows up after action, not before. Start tired. Start unsure. Start anyway.

slides.title: Ways [[3–4]]
items: You do it alone because asking feels embarrassing.
You punish yourself after slips instead of learning.

slides.title: Make it [[easier]]
items: Close every backdoor today.
Act first, feel motivated later.
Tell one person you're quitting p*rn.
After a slip, write one lesson — then move on.
